subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What security and ownership boundary should the browser-login handoff surface use before implementation?
rationale: The requested UI would expose and possibly control authenticated browser state, and current related work leaves open whether the surface belongs in first-party Control UI, the browser plugin, or a generic plugin UI extension path.

options.title: Read-only-first operator handoff panel
options.body: Implement a secured operator-scoped panel that shows status, URL/title, tabs, and screenshots by default while requiring explicit user action for focus, navigation, clicks, credentials, submit actions, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer implementation until the generic plugin UI entry-point contract lands, then make the browser plugin own the panel under that reviewed API.

options.title: Defer the panel
options.body: Keep the current CLI/RPC/screenshot workflows and leave this issue as product backlog until browser handoff becomes a scheduled product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first operator handoff panel
recommendation.body: Implement a secured operator-scoped panel that shows status, URL/title, tabs, and screenshots by default while requiring explicit user action for focus, navigation, clicks, credentials, submit actions, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is already the strongest routing signal from the issue discussion and recent browser/UI history.
